plan.title: Feedback gets a natural thanks and "the team's on it"

context.text: Kalimera Jordan! 30 minutes around the park at 6 today. What's the plan to make it happen?

transcript.text: feedback: the 9am text is too early for me
Thanks, Jordan. I passed that along to the team word for word, and they're on it. Your run is still set for 6 pm today, 30 minutes at the park. Send me the Strava screenshot when you're done.

checks.reason: Thanks Jordan, says the team's on it, makes no specific change promise, and steers back to today's run in a short line.

conversation.reason: ZOH acknowledged the feedback, thanked Jordan, said the team's on it, promised no change, and steered back to the 6 pm run.

grade.summary: ZOH handled the feedback path well: it thanked Jordan, passed the note to the team, and promised no specific change. Its phrasing 'passed that along to the team word for word' is slightly mechanical, but it stayed short and returned to today's run.
